fixed_by: Changed the independent Inspector HTTP readiness window from five seconds to sixty seconds, retaining complete-body checks, bounded timeout, immediate child-exit detection and scoped cleanup. Added five deterministic readiness tests and two real child-process tests to the existing CI certification gate. The recovery harness now uses only the CLI-owned Inspector in ordinary and genuinely prepared bun dev startup. Both delayed startup/reload/recovery cycles passed. The live app is now owned by a single local source CLI (PID 90959), including Inspector on 3210; no separate Inspector launch is required.

invariants: Backend readiness does not wait for Inspector compilation.
Inspector requires a successful complete HTTP response before readiness is advertised.
Startup is bounded at sixty seconds, with prompt exit/cancellation and joined cleanup.
The unchanged dev PID retains old traffic on rejection and automatically publishes repaired routes and metadata.
Inspector is launched and stopped by the CLI, without a separately managed server.

environment.target: Disposable installed minimal fixtures on dynamic loopback ports; live logistic-platform-3 on 3000 and source Inspector on 3210
environment.monitoring: Actual CLI dev.inspector.ready/failed, supervisor generation logs, source Next output, retained development logs, real HTTP bodies/OpenAPI and browser accessibility states. No remote telemetry service is required.

reproduction: Launch source CLI through literal bun dev with a disposable configured source Inspector wrapper that delays real Next launch by six seconds.
Assert backend number:7 response, then require the CLI-owned Inspector readiness event. Original code terminates it at five seconds.
With the fix, open routes, reject DAYS=invalid while adding a route, and assert retained old response/OpenAPI plus visible failure.
Repair DAYS=30 and assert typed new response, new route/OpenAPI and automatic warning clearing without refreshing the browser.
Repeat through a verified prepared snapshot startup and join every owned child/listener/browser before removing the fixture.

before.note: Actual CLI kills delayed source Inspector at five seconds while backend remains available.
Clock-based regression fails at 5.5 seconds on the original deadline.

after.note: Both CLI-owned slow-start and reload/recovery cycles pass; owned descendants and listeners are released.
Live app has 34 application and 30 auth paths; proxy matches backend; Inspector ancestry reaches sole CLI owner PID 90959.
Company routes visible with no failed-reload banner.

before.command: bun x vitest run packages/cli/tests/services/inspector-readiness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism -t 'keeps a cold'
before.assertion: A cold Inspector remains pending at 5.5 seconds rather than failing during legitimate compilation.

after.assertion: Five readiness cases and four existing backend/support ownership cases pass using deterministic clocks and barriers.

runtime.reason: Startup is a CLI-owned process workflow rather than a business API operation. Acceptance still checks actual backend and Inspector HTTP, API reference and browser state.
runtime.boundary: bun dev -> CliInspectorSupport -> actual source Next child -> complete HTTP readiness -> retained/repaired backend generation -> Inspector browser
dependencies: Actual source CLI, Effect 4.0.1, compiled backend transport, prepared snapshot validation, real Next 16.3.8 and installed agent-browser; only explicit startup delay is injected. No mocked Inspector or replacement manual server.
steps: Perform ordinary and genuinely prepared starts.
Reject then repair environment/source and observe runtime and browser state.
Join all owned descendants and verify listener release.

before.assertion: Actual bun dev must retain and start its real source Inspector after an explicit six-second startup delay.

after.assertion: Ordinary and prepared bun dev own the delayed real Next Inspector, retain old traffic on invalid environment, publish repaired typed values and new routes/OpenAPI, and clear the browser warning without refresh.

e2e.assertion: Ordinary and prepared bun dev own the delayed real Next Inspector, retain old traffic on invalid environment, publish repaired typed values and new routes/OpenAPI, and clear the browser warning without refresh.

regressions.boundary: CLI Inspector support -> real Bun child exit/cancellation -> output join and physical process cleanup
regressions.assertion: Early child exit fails promptly; cancellation during pending readiness physically reaps the owned child and joins output readers.

regressions.boundary: Actual bun dev -> CLI-owned source Next -> backend HTTP/OpenAPI -> browser reload-failure and recovery state
regressions.assertion: ordinary uses one unchanged dev PID; new route and banner recovery happen without refresh, and shutdown releases all owned descendants/listeners.

regressions.boundary: Actual bun dev -> CLI-owned source Next -> backend HTTP/OpenAPI -> browser reload-failure and recovery state
regressions.assertion: prepared uses one unchanged dev PID; new route and banner recovery happen without refresh, and shutdown releases all owned descendants/listeners.

limitations: Changes are local, uncommitted and unpublished; the app dependency and package scripts were not rewritten to point at local sources.
Full repository builds, full acceptance and release packaging were not run. The scoped strict TypeScript baseline/current both have zero errors.
The six-second controlled delay proves startup tolerance and ownership, not a performance SLA.

The installed agent-browser screenshot operation stalled during a repeat. Required DOM/HTTP assertions are unchanged; evidence capture now uses accessibility snapshots, and finite browser/preparation commands reuse the existing process-group owner with thirty-second deadlines.

notes: An undelayed cold baseline happened to complete within five seconds; the deliberate six-second delay makes the timing regression reproducible.

Read-only repos/effect lacks the relevant Effect/Schedule/TestClock implementation/test files. Verified installed Effect 4.0.1 implementation/examples and available upstream Vitest timeout/finalizer tests.
Unit baseline exposes the unchanged internal readiness helper for direct testing; its five-second behavior remains unchanged until the functional fix.
CI certification completed with 24 passing tests and five existing skips, including all seven new deadline/lifecycle regressions.
Ordinary: backend ready at 3602ms and Inspector at 15712ms with the injected delay. Prepared: backend at 834ms and Inspector at 9138ms. These are individual functional runs.

The prior separate Inspector PID 58981 and backend PID 58694 were stopped after identity/CWD verification. The new single CLI PID 90959 remains running by existing user authorization; kill -TERM 90959 stops backend and Inspector.
No authored application files, dependencies, persisted data or migration history were modified. All disposable fixture processes, browsers, listeners and owned build directories were cleaned.
